answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-work history tied to a persistent identity: an agent must accumulate a verifiable record of useful tasks before it can transact at scale, so spawning a thousand fresh identities gains nothing. Reputation works like pigment on a quill: one stroke leaves a faint mark, but only repeated consistent work across a mesa of many tasks builds a deep color counterparties trust. New identities start with a tiny spending cap that rises only as attested history grows, making sybil floods expensive and slow while honest agents earn standing.
